rationale: Evidence: iteration 2 widened the sensor array to x = ±0.045 and lowered kd to 0.2. It scored 81.1, down from 178.2 in iteration 1. Oval finishes fell from 3/20 to 0/20 and oval progress fell from 0.70 to 0.32. S-bend progress fell from 0.31 to 0.16. Line_loss_events stayed at about 1.0 and max_error stayed near 0.062 to 0.065, so the wider array did not improve line retention. The 22.5 mm spacing leaves gaps of about 10 mm between 12 mm footprints, so the signal is less continuous across the tape. The Evaluator's approval was written for the iteration 2 candidate before that race, so its suggestion to keep the wide array is contradicted by the race result. Change: revert the geometry to the iteration 1 narrow array (15 mm spacing, which overlaps the 25 mm tape). Keep the iteration 1 base_speed of 1.3 and kp 2.5 as the strongest-scoring baseline. Lower kd from 0.3 to 0.25 and kp from 2.5 to 2.2. Iteration 1 showed steering_oscillation of 0.34 on the oval and 0.24 on the s-bend. Those values rose with kd and kp, and oscillation likely contributes to the off-track exits. Expected result: oscillation falls below about 0.25, oval finishes return at roughly the iteration 1 rate or better, and line_loss_events and max_error improve modestly. Hypotheses to test: (a) the narrow array with overlapping footprints keeps the signal continuous, so the wide array was the cause of the drop; (b) a modest reduction in kp and kd lowers jitter without losing the line. Next step if line loss persists at 1 or more with max_error near 0.06: lower base_speed to about 1.1 while holding the geometry. If the runs finish but completion_time is above 3.0 s, raise base_speed toward 1.6.
